Name: Taj Mahal
Description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna. Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

Name: Agra Fort
Description: A historical fort in Agra. It was the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal Dynasty until 1638.

Name: Ajanta Caves
Description: Rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE. Famous for their ancient paintings and sculptures.

Name: Ellora Caves
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments carved out of rock. Includes the famous Kailasa temple.

Name: Red Fort
Description: A historic fort in Old Delhi that served as the main residence of the Mughal Emperors. Symbol of India's independence.

Name: Qutub Minar
Description: A 73-metre tall minaret and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built in the early 13th century.

Name: Humayun's Tomb
Description: The tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun. First garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent and inspired the Taj Mahal.

Name: Konark Sun Temple
Description: A 13th-century Sun Temple at Konark shaped as a gigantic chariot with elaborately carved stone wheels, pillars, and walls.

Name: Mahabodhi Temple
Description: A Buddhist temple marking the location where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment and became the Buddha.

Name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
Description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples famous for their nagara-style architectural symbolism and erotic sculptures.

Name: Hampi Monuments
Description: The ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire. Features ancient temples, forts, and other structures spread across a landscape.

Name: Fatehpur Sikri
Description: A city built by Mughal Emperor Akbar. Known for its Mughal architecture and historical significance.

Name: Elephanta Caves
Description: A network of sculpted caves on Elephanta Island. Famous for rock-cut art and sculptures dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
Description: A historic railway station in Mumbai and an outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture.

Name: Pattadakal Monuments
Description: A complex of 7th and 8th century Hindu and Jain temples showcasing early Chalukyan architecture.

Name: Sanchi Stupa
Description: A Buddhist complex famous for its Great Stupa. Built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

Name: Sundarbans National Park
Description: The largest mangrove forest in the world. Home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

Name: Nanda Devi National Park
Description: A national park dominated by the Nanda Devi peak, the second highest mountain in India.

Name: Kaziranga National Park
Description: A national park famous for its one-horned rhinoceros population. Also home to tigers, elephants, and various bird species.

Name: Manas Wildlife Sanctuary
Description: A UNESCO Natural World Heritage site and a Project Tiger reserve. Known for its rare and endangered endemic wildlife.

Name: Keoladeo National Park
Description: A famous avifauna sanctuary that hosts thousands of birds, especially during winter. Also known as Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.

Name: Churches and Convents of Goa
Description: A collection of churches and convents built by Portuguese colonial rulers. Includes the Basilica of Bom Jesus.

Name: Great Living Chola Temples
Description: Three great temples built by the Chola dynasty: Brihadisvara at Thanjavur, Brihadisvara at Gangaikondacholapuram, and Airavatesvara at Darasuram.

Name: Mahabalipuram Monuments
Description: A collection of 7th and 8th century religious monuments. Famous for Shore Temple and rock-cut sculptures.

Name: Mountain Railways of India
Description: A collective UNESCO site including Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Nilgiri Mountain Railway, and Kalka-Shimla Railway.

Name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
Description: A concentration of largely unexcavated archaeological, historic, and living cultural heritage properties.

Name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
Description: An astronomical observation site built by Maharaja Jai Singh II. Features the world's largest stone sundial.

Name: Western Ghats
Description: A mountain range running parallel to the western coast of India. One of the world's eight 'hottest hotspots' of biological diversity.

Name: Hill Forts of Rajasthan
Description: A serial nomination of six majestic forts in Rajasthan including Amber Fort, Chittorgarh, Gagron Fort, Jaisalmer Fort, Kumbhalgarh, and Ranthambore.

Name: Rani Ki Vav
Description: A stepwell located on the banks of Saraswati River. Built as a memorial to a king by his widowed queen.

Name: Great Himalayan National Park
Description: A national park in the western Himalayas. Known for its biodiversity including numerous flora, fauna, and mammals.

Name: Nalanda Mahavihara
Description: Archaeological site of an ancient university and Buddhist monastery. One of the first great universities in recorded history.

Name: Khangchendzonga National Park
Description: A national park featuring the world's third highest peak. A sacred landscape with cultural and religious significance.

Name: The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier
Description: Capitol Complex designed by Le Corbusier. An outstanding contribution to the Modern Movement in architecture.

Name: Historic City of Ahmadabad
Description: The walled city of Ahmadabad founded in the 15th century. A blend of Hindu, Islamic, and Jain architecture.

Name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
Description: A collection of 19th-century Victorian Gothic and 20th-century Art Deco buildings. Unique blend of architectural styles.

Name: Jaipur City
Description: The Pink City of Jaipur, founded in 1727. Known for its unique urban planning and architectural harmony.

Name: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple
Description: A 13th-century temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. Known for its engineering, floating bricks, and intricate sculptures.

Name: Dholavira: A Harappan City
Description: One of the most prominent archaeological sites of Indus Valley Civilization. Features sophisticated water management and urban planning.

Name: Hoysala Sacred Ensembles
Description: Three Hoysala temples representing the peak of 12th-13th century Hoysala architecture. Known for detailed stone carvings.

Name: Moidams - Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
Description: Funerary mounds of Ahom royalty. Represents unique burial traditions and architectural heritage of medieval Assam.

Name: Santiniketan
Description: Established by Rabindranath Tagore. An educational institution representing the synthesis of Indian and global traditions.
